evals.name: resource-crud-design
evals.prompt: I need to design the API for managing ad campaigns. Each campaign belongs to an advertiser, and we need the usual create / read / update / list / delete. Write me the .proto — the service and the messages.
evals.expected_output: A resource-oriented proto with the five standard methods, a name-based resource identifier, parent-scoped collection, pagination on List, and a field mask on Update.
expectations: The Campaign message carries a string name field as its resource identifier following the pattern advertisers/{advertiser}/campaigns/{campaign}, rather than a bare id field.
The service defines the five standard methods named GetCampaign, ListCampaigns, CreateCampaign, UpdateCampaign and DeleteCampaign, each with its own request message.
ListCampaignsRequest includes parent, page_size and page_token; ListCampaignsResponse includes a repeated campaigns field and next_page_token.
UpdateCampaignRequest includes a google.protobuf.FieldMask update_mask field.
CreateCampaignRequest includes parent and the campaign resource (and a campaign_id field, or an explanation of server-assigned ids).

The google.api.http bindings use the correct shapes, not merely present annotations: get on /v1/{name=advertisers/*/campaigns/*}, post on the parent collection with body: "campaign", and patch keyed on {campaign.name=...}.
The name field is annotated (google.api.field_behavior) = IDENTIFIER — not REQUIRED, which is the common mistake — and the message carries a google.api.resource option declaring its pattern and type.
The parent field carries a google.api.resource_reference with child_type (or type) rather than being an unannotated string.
create_time and update_time are present and annotated OUTPUT_ONLY, and any enum's zero value is named *_UNSPECIFIED.
The proto package ends in a major version (e.g. acme.advertising.v1) rather than being unversioned.

Every import the file needs is present, in alphabetical order: google/api/client.proto whenever method_signature is used and google/protobuf/empty.proto whenever Delete returns Empty. The old worked example omitted client.proto and with-skill answers copied the gap.

Every request field carries a field_behavior, including page_size and page_token (OPTIONAL), update_mask (OPTIONAL) and the user-settable fields of Campaign, since the resource is sent in Create and Update.
The answer validates with api-linter (runs it, or says it is not installed and gives the go install command) rather than presenting a compile, or nothing, as validation.

evals.name: custom-method-and-lro
evals.prompt: We need to add an 'archive' operation to our campaigns API. Archiving moves a lot of historical data around so it takes several minutes to finish — the client can't just block on it. How should I model that in the proto, and why?
evals.expected_output: A custom method ArchiveCampaign bound with a colon suffix, returning google.longrunning.Operation with operation_info declaring response and metadata types, plus reasoning about when a custom method is appropriate.
expectations: The method is a custom method named ArchiveCampaign taking an ArchiveCampaignRequest whose identifier field is name, with name annotated REQUIRED and carrying a google.api.resource_reference.
The HTTP binding uses the colon-suffix form for custom methods, e.g. post: "/v1/{name=advertisers/*/campaigns/*}:archive".
Because the operation is long-running, the method returns google.longrunning.Operation rather than the resource directly.
The response declares google.longrunning.operation_info with both response_type and metadata_type.
A metadata message is actually defined (not just named) carrying progress information such as create_time, end_time, or a percent/stage field.
The archival lifecycle is modelled on the resource itself — an OUTPUT_ONLY state or lifecycle enum — so clients can observe the result, rather than the RPC being the only expression of it.

The response explains why this is a custom method rather than a standard one (the behaviour doesn't map onto Get/List/Create/Update/Delete) and, if it discusses alternatives, says why Update-with-state or soft-delete were rejected.

Any proto it writes imports google/api/client.proto when it uses method_signature and google/longrunning/operations.proto for Operation, and it validates with api-linter (or names the install command) rather than stopping at a compile.

evals.name: review-nonconforming-proto
evals.expected_output: A review flagging the enum zero value, id-instead-of-name, method naming, missing pagination, plural/singular collection naming, and the versionless package.
expectations: Flags that the Status enum's zero value must be STATUS_UNSPECIFIED rather than a meaningful default like ACTIVE.
Flags that the resource identifier should be a string name field following a resource-name pattern, not an int64 id.
Flags the method naming — rpc getItem should be PascalCase GetItem, and DeleteItemById should be DeleteItem.
Flags that ListItems is missing pagination — page_size and page_token on the request, next_page_token on the response — and that limit is the wrong field name.
Flags the collection naming: the List method and its messages should be plural (ListItems, ListItemsRequest, ListItemsResponse), and Req/Resp should be spelled Request/Response.
Flags that the package inventory lacks a major version and should be inventory.v1.

Flags that DeleteItem returning Item is wrong and should return google.protobuf.Empty (or, if soft delete is intended, says so and adds Undelete). This is judged separately from the package-version finding.
Flags the redundant is_deleted boolean field (soft-delete state belongs in the enum or is expressed via the standard delete semantics).
Flags that the service has no google.api.http bindings at all, so none of the RPCs are reachable over REST.
Flags the absence of google.api.resource / field_behavior annotations, or the total absence of doc comments on the service, messages and fields.

evals.name: extend-existing-message
evals.prompt: Can you add two fields to the Job message in protos/acme/jobs/v1/jobs.proto? max_retries — how many times we retry a failed run. 0 means never retry, and if it's not set at all we fall back to the project default of 3. And owned_by_team, the team that owns the job (just the team slug for now). Keep it consistent with the rest of the file please, other teams generate clients from this.
evals.expected_output: Job gains max_retries and a preposition-free owning team field on the next free numbers (7 and 8), max_retries uses proto3 optional, the reply lists each place the new fields differ from the file's convention and asks which to follow, says the change is non-breaking, and validates with api-linter reporting only findings on the changed lines.
expectations: The new fields take numbers 7 and 8: not 5, which is reserved, and not 100 or above after the 97-99 block. The reply shows it read the reserved range rather than guessing.
max_retries is declared `optional int32 max_retries`, because 0 (never retry) and unset (use the default of 3) mean different things. A plain int32 or a google.protobuf.Int32Value wrapper fails this.
The owner field drops the preposition, e.g. owning_team or team, and the reply says why it differs from the requested owned_by_team.
It does not rename expiry_time to expire_time or otherwise touch existing fields, because that would break generated clients; it may point out the expiry_time deviation as a note.

The reply lists each place the new code departs from the file's existing convention (for example the field name, any field_behavior added where the file has none) one line each, and asks whether the user wants the repo's convention instead, rather than silently picking one.
The reply states that adding the two fields is a non-breaking change.

It validates with api-linter (runs it with -I for the googleapis imports, or says it is not installed and gives the go install command) and reports only findings on the lines it changed, not the dozen pre-existing ones. A buf build or protoc compile alone does not pass.

evals.name: breaking-change-check
evals.expected_output: A per-change verdict: the rename, adding optional, moving fields into a oneof and removing total_cents are breaking; notes and CANCELLED are additive. It also flags customer_name misusing the _name suffix and proposes a v1-safe path (add new fields alongside, deprecate the old ones) or a v2.
expectations: Judges the customer to customer_name rename as breaking even though the field number is unchanged: the JSON/REST field name and every generated accessor change.
Judges adding `optional` to quantity as breaking for generated code (for example Go and other languages switch to a pointer or has-accessor), not as safe because the wire format is the same.
Judges moving coupon_code and gift_card_code into a oneof as breaking, because a message that set both is now silently reduced to one.
Judges removing total_cents as breaking for existing clients that read it, while noting that reserving 7 is the right way to retire a number.
Judges notes = 6 and the CANCELLED enum value as additive, with a caution that old clients will see an unrecognised enum value.
Flags customer_name: the _name suffix is reserved for resource names (AIP-148), so if customer is a resource it should stay customer with a resource_reference, and if not it needs another name.
Proposes a path that keeps v1 compatible, such as adding total alongside total_cents and marking total_cents deprecated, keeping customer as it is, and leaving the oneof change for v2.

evals.name: compiles-but-not-linted
evals.prompt: buf build is green on protos/acme/notes/v1/notes_service.proto so I think we're good — can you give it a quick once-over before I merge? It's a new service, nothing depends on it yet.
evals.expected_output: Does not take the green compile as approval: runs api-linter (or gives the install command) and reports the findings, notably missing field_behavior on page_size, page_token and the Note fields, REQUIRED instead of IDENTIFIER on name, the trailing comment, the uncommented GetNote and name, unsorted imports, is_pinned (should be pinned), create_time missing OUTPUT_ONLY, and says the file is not ready to merge.
expectations: Says plainly that a passing buf build only proves the file compiles, and validates with api-linter: runs it with -I for the googleapis imports, or says it is not installed and gives `go install github.com/googleapis/api-linter/cmd/api-linter@latest`.
Flags that Note.name should be annotated IDENTIFIER, not REQUIRED.
Flags the missing field_behavior on page_size and page_token (OPTIONAL) and on the user-settable Note fields, since Note is sent in CreateNote. Saying field_behavior is merely recommended fails this.
Flags create_time as missing OUTPUT_ONLY.
Flags the trailing comment on name (it should be a leading `// Format: users/{user}/notes/{note}` comment) and the missing comment on the GetNote RPC.
Flags the imports as out of alphabetical order (timestamp.proto is first).
Flags is_pinned, which should be pinned per AIP-140.
Concludes that the file is not ready to merge as is, and since nothing depends on it yet, says this is the cheap moment to fix it.
